issues.legal_issue: Whether income primarily earmarked for the testator’s near relations constitutes income of a public charitable trust.
material_facts: The will divided the income of the trust property into four portions: one portion was set aside for public charitable purposes, two portions were for assistance to specified relations and their dependants, and one portion was reserved for augmenting the trust corpus.
The assistance for relatives included food, clothing, education and, where appropriate, a lump-sum payment; the trustees were directed to give special care to certain descendants.
The will directed that the portions intended for relatives would be used for charitable purposes if the descendants became extinct or the specified purpose became impossible to perform.
The appeal challenged the determination that the portions primarily earmarked for relatives did not constitute a public charitable trust.
issues.conclusion: The portions of income primarily earmarked for the benefit of the testator’s near relations could not be considered income of a public charitable trust; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Section 4(b) of the Kerala Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, the Court held that the part of the trust primarily earmarked for the benefit of the testator’s near relations was not a public charitable trust. It followed the ratio of Trustees of Gordhandas Govindram Family Trust, Bombay v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay, which it described as addressing a similar provision.

predicates.public_charitable_trust_tax_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether trust income qualifies as income of a public charitable trust for tax purposes.
predicates.income_primarily_earmarked_for_testators: The trust instrument primarily directs the income in issue to benefit the settlor’s or testator’s near relatives.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns the tax classification of public charitable trust income and the income is primarily earmarked for the testator’s near relatives, that allocation is not treated as a public charitable trust.
